A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DMPO research work. All 22 pages of v1 and 27 pages of v2, including references and appendices, are readable. Text, equations, tables, figures, and relocated material support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original DMPO fine-tuning results on four reasoning benchmarks, training reward curves, and a Sudoku weight-baseline ablation. Appendix C supplies experimental details and generated examples.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds evaluated model variants, training-efficiency comparisons, hyperparameter ablations, and rollout-entropy results in Section 4 and Appendix C.3.

M1.justification: The WDCE/WDDO objectives, importance weights, three weight baselines, and core update algorithm remain unchanged. v2 adds Fast-dLLM with approximate KV caching and confidence-based sampling as an implemented rollout-generation option alongside random-order sampling (Section 4 and Appendix C.2), providing a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSM8K, MATH500, three-number Countdown, and 4-by-4 Sudoku. s1k already appears in v1's d1 training pipeline. The added initialization, sampler, and hyperparameter experiments do not introduce a new task, domain, or represented data population.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds cGRPO-LLaDA as an evaluated comparator across the four benchmarks. Coupled-GRPO was discussed but not included in v1's reported comparison. Dream-Instruct, LLaDA-Instruct, LLaDA-1.5, and d1-LLaDA remain.

E3.justification: The main zero-shot evaluation at 128, 256, and 512 tokens is retained. v2 adds SFT/DPO-checkpoint initialization arms, a compute-matched rollout-sampler comparison, and fixed-batch-size Countdown sweeps over N=4–32 and F=1–24 using six-hour and eight-hour budgets. It also specifies an entropy-evaluation protocol with N=16, F=8, and measurements every ten generations.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained but revised Sudoku weight-baseline study, v2 investigates compatibility with prior post-training, sampler efficiency, sensitivity to rollout count and buffer reuse, and rollout entropy (Table 1 and Figures 5, 7–9). These substantially expand the questions tested. v1's reward-dynamics analysis is retained as v2 Figure 6 rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions already display shaded training curves without defining the bands or reporting repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2 extends this existing plotting practice but introduces no identifiable new uncertainty-estimation or statistical-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises reported DMPO-LLaDA Countdown accuracies from 64.84/75.78/79.69 to 67.19/80.86/82.81 at 128/256/512 tokens; its other nine scores and existing comparator rows remain unchanged. Three new model rows and additional efficiency, sensitivity, and entropy findings substantially expand the results. Section 4 newly reports comparable reward using 1.8 versus 5.78 PF-days; the revised Countdown scores should not be interpreted as isolated same-training-setting gains.

T1.justification: New Appendix B.1 introduces CTMC and path-measure definitions, Lemma B.1, and a stochastic-control derivation connecting WDCE to path-space KL matching. The earlier zero-temperature extension, variance-reduction argument, and WDDO proof are retained and renumbered. The new gamma(t)=1/t schedule, however, conflicts with the stated fully masked t=0 initialization and 1-t masking convention.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace headline improvements of 42.9%/55.8% with 54.3%/66.41%. The latter match 256-token Countdown accuracy-point gaps against d1 and LLaDA-Instruct, rather than the earlier approximately cross-length-average gaps. The central distribution-matching, weight-baseline, and reasoning-without-SFT contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning compatibility with SFT/DPO, generation parallelism explaining rollout-count timing, and sequence-level importance weighting contributing to stability. It also discusses late-training instability under heavy rollout reuse and interprets the new entropy measurements as supporting diversity preservation. The principal limitation to the LLaDA family and four elementary reasoning benchmarks remains.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 newly specifies rollout temperatures of 0 for random-order sampling and 0.2 for Fast-dLLM, plus individual-weight-baseline assignments for the new DMPO-SFT and DMPO-LLaDA-1.5 variants. Added analyses document their hardware budgets and entropy-measurement procedure. Most existing implementation settings and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Campbell et al. (2024), Generative Flows on Discrete State-Spaces, and Ren et al. (2025a), How Discrete and Continuous Diffusion Meet, supporting the CTMC derivation. It makes the connection to already-cited DRAKES and MDNS more explicit. Most related-work positioning is retained; numerous venue updates concern the same cited works.

P1.justification: Existing prose receives local editing, headings and terminology are refined, and random-order autoregressive sampling gains the ROAR abbreviation. The reward-dynamics discussion moves to Appendix C.3, and appendix subsections are reorganized around new material. Most existing narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 substantially changes typography and the width of the single-column layout. Figure 1 moves to the opening page and gains model series; Table 1 expands from five to eight model rows. Algorithm 1 and the original reward-dynamics figure move to the appendices, while four new figures display efficiency, hyperparameter, and entropy analyses. Existing plots are also reformatted.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical support for important advantages that v1 largely motivated prospectively: compute efficiency, effective rollout reuse, and diversity preservation receive direct tests in Figures 5 and 7–9. The added cGRPO comparison and post-trained initializations further improve evaluation. These address substantial validation gaps. The benefit is chiefly empirical: uncertainty bands remain unexplained, and the new stochastic-control appendix contains a time-schedule inconsistency, limiting the theoretical gain.
